reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows ML can predict yield strength with moderate error, but it does not provide any support for the key premises about reduced-order physics, explicit hierarchical descriptors, or fracture toughness prediction. The claimed 20% error reduction and order-of-magnitude speedup are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: ML surrogate models can predict yield strength of HEAs with ~11–13% error at room temperature
Reduced-order physics estimates (e.g., effective medium) can provide useful elastic/yield inputs
Explicit microstructural descriptors of hierarchical heterostructures can be constructed and fed to ML
Incorporating such descriptors into ML improves accuracy and efficiency over CALPHAD/first-principles
The approach can predict fracture toughness, a property not addressed in the cited evidence
